title: Bladder ultrasound with residual urine
also: bladder scan before and after peeing
what: The doctor looks at your bladder with ultrasound, first when it is full, then right after you go to the toilet. This shows how much urine is left.
why: For frequent urges to pee, a weak stream, a feeling that the bladder is not empty, prostate problems, or frequent bladder infections.
duration: usually 15 to 20 minutes, plus time to fill your bladder
tell_doctor: If it is hard to hold your urine for long, or you leak urine
If you have a catheter, or have had bladder or prostate surgery

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: Usually, 1 to 1.5 hours before the scan, drink 1 to 1.5 liters of still water or tea.

prepare.title: Toilet
prepare.text: After that, do not go to the toilet. When you arrive, your bladder should feel full, but you can still hold it.

prepare.title: If you can't wait
prepare.text: Tell the front desk. Sometimes they can take you sooner. You can also empty a little and drink more water.

bring: A tissue to wipe off the gel
steps: You lie on your back with your lower belly bare
The doctor puts on gel and looks at your full bladder
You are asked to go to the toilet and empty your bladder completely
You come back right away, and the doctor looks at your bladder again
The second look shows how much urine is left
feel: The probe presses on your full bladder. You may feel the urge to pee, but it does not hurt
after: The gel is wiped off, and you can go back to your day right away
You usually get the report right away
red_flags: If you cannot pee at all and your lower belly feels swollen and painful, this needs urgent care. Call emergency services

faq.q: How much water should I drink before a bladder ultrasound?
faq.a: Usually 1 to 1.5 liters over an hour to an hour and a half, without going to the toilet. Your clinic will tell you exactly.

faq.q: How much residual urine is normal?
faq.a: Usually very little. Your doctor will explain what your numbers mean, based on your symptoms and age.

reminders.text: Bladder ultrasound soon. 1 to 1.5 hours before it, drink 1 to 1.5 liters of water and do not go to the toilet.
